title: Copilot in Excel & the Analyst Agent

questions.question: What does Copilot in Excel need in order to work with your data?
options: The workbook saved to the cloud (such as OneDrive) and the data formatted as a table or supported range
The workbook stored only on your local hard drive
The data pasted in from a web page every time
The workbook converted to a PDF first
questions.explanation: Copilot in Excel needs the file saved to the cloud (OneDrive or SharePoint) and the data formatted as a table or supported range so it can read and analyze it.

questions.question: What can Copilot in Excel do with formulas?
options: Generate formulas and calculated columns, and explain what an existing formula does
Explain existing formulas but never create new ones
Only perform calculations by writing VBA macros
Nothing; Copilot cannot work with formulas
questions.explanation: Copilot can generate formulas and new calculated columns from your data, and it can also explain how an existing formula works.

questions.question: When is the Analyst agent especially useful?
options: When your data spans multiple files that are not yet in Excel, so it can explore and consolidate them for you
Only when all data is already in a single open worksheet
Only after you manually merge every file into one workbook
Only if you write SQL to combine the data sources
questions.explanation: The Analyst agent is built for data that spans multiple files that are not yet in Excel: it explores and compares those datasets and consolidates them for you instead of making you combine files manually.

questions.question: How does Copilot in Excel with Python handle an advanced analysis such as a forecast?
options: You describe the problem in plain language, and Copilot generates and runs the Python code, returning results in your workbook
You must write all the Python code yourself; Copilot only explains it
It runs the analysis in a separate web app, never in your workbook
It uses the R language instead of Python
questions.explanation: With Copilot in Excel with Python, you describe the analysis in plain language and Copilot generates and runs the Python code for you, returning the results directly in your workbook.

questions.question: Select all the ways Copilot in Excel can present insights about your data.
options: As charts
As PivotTables
As summaries of trends
By highlighting outliers
By emailing your workbook to other organizations
questions.explanation: Copilot in Excel can surface insights as charts, PivotTables, summaries, trends, and outliers. It does not send your workbook to other organizations.

questions.question: Select all that the Analyst agent can do with your data.
options: Calculate statistics
Identify trends
Show outliers
Return a plain-language report that can include charts and tables
Automatically send emails to stakeholders
questions.explanation: The Analyst agent calculates statistics, identifies trends, shows outliers, and returns a plain-language report that can include charts and tables. It does not send emails on its own.
